basis: Autoinflammatory disease defined by panniculitis, uveitis and systemic granulomatous inflammation; other organ frequencies are unspecified.
Steroid-associated ocular hypertension/borderline glaucoma; the eye is the defined disease site.
Cobalamin metabolic defect; developmental neurologic injury commonly exceeds 30%, and CKD affects roughly half or more in cblB disease; cardiomyopathy reported in one patient is insufficient.
Inherited proteostasis disorder principally expressing Paget bone disease or inclusion body myopathy; dementia and ALS are less frequent across this umbrella.
Renal tubular wasting with phosphate and acid-base disturbances; rickets in 19/19 causes skeletal damage. Secondary hypertension is separately coded; emphysema 3/12 is below 30%.
Germ-cell neoplasm of the ovary, a reproductive site; endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Hereditary colorectal carcinoma defines the affected organ; other cancer risks do not establish direct involvement.
Clonal B-cell leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma; lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; lissencephaly and muscular dystrophy in 6/6, retinal dysplasia or glaucoma each in 2/6.
Defined by leukoencephalopathy, cerebral ischemic injury and retinal degeneration; no separate vascular disorder established, and scoliosis frequency is unspecified.
Premature fusion of metopic and sagittal skull sutures; neurologic injury is not inherent to nonsyndromic craniosynostosis.
Inherited erythrocyte membrane disorder; most patients are asymptomatic, and skin ulcers and gallstones are minority complications.
Acute myeloid leukemia involving marrow and myeloid blood cells; the KIT mutation does not establish another affected organ.
APOB lipid disorder; hepatic steatosis with biochemical injury commonly affects over 30%. Severe intestinal, neurologic and retinal disease chiefly affects the biallelic minority.
Cobalamin metabolic defect; intellectual disability/movement impairment and megaloblastic marrow changes are each reported in 80-99%.
Sensory/autonomic neuropathy with defining anhidrosis and frequent sweat-gland aplasia; fractures, osteomyelitis and oral injuries are secondary complications.
Purely psychiatric mood-disorder umbrella; the brain-disorder ancestor does not establish neurologic damage.
Closed spinal dysraphism involving vertebral posterior elements and the neural-tube developmental spectrum; additional functional organ damage is not universal.
Cutaneous mast-cell proliferation causing extensive blistering and erythroderma; cardiorespiratory arrest occurs in only 5-29%.
Acute inflammation of tooth-supporting tissues, typically driven by bacterial infection; periodontal tissues belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Umbrella for congenital infections; organ injury varies substantially by pathogen, with no additional organ established across most of the group.
Intellectual disability and broad digits define syndrome; strabismus in 7/11 and renal abnormalities in 30-79%. Dental crowding alone does not establish tissue damage.
Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia affects vertebral and epiphyseal skeletal development; the gene association alone does not establish vascular involvement.
Benign vascular tumor arising in the liver; the endocrine-neoplasm ancestor does not make this an endocrine disorder.
Inherited hemorrhagic diathesis is a coagulation disorder; no specific additional organ damage is established.
